153	- API endpoints: Any list endpoints missing pagination?
154	- Async/Sync: Any operations that should be asynchronous but are synchronous?
155	- Frontend: Any unnecessary re-renders? (React: missing useMemo/useCallback; check render-triggering state changes)
156	- Memory/CPU: Any unbounded loops or potential memory leaks? (Missing cleanup in useEffect, unclosed streams)
157	
158	Produce: status per check item with severity tag for any findings.
159	
160	> **Core principle**: Measure before optimizing. Flag patterns, do not prescribe specific optimizations without benchmark data.
161	
162	For deeper checks, the review skill also provides `references/security-checklist.md` and `references/performance-checklist.md` if more scrutiny is warranted.
163	
164	**f. Assemble Review Report**
165	
166	Format for terminal display and GitHub issue:
167	```markdown
168	## Review Report: Group N, {group name}
169	
170	### Anti-Rationalization Check
171	Confirmed no excuses are influencing review judgment:
172	- [x] "It runs" — Review covers readability, architecture, security, performance
173	- [x] "Small change" — All changes reviewed regardless of size
174	
175	### Code Quality
176	| File | Finding | Severity | Comment |
177	|------|---------|----------|---------|
178	| path/file.py | Clean structure, consistent naming | ℹ️ | — |
179	
180	### Architecture
181	| Check | Status | Note |
182	|-------|--------|------|
183	| Follows existing patterns | ✅ | — |
184	| Module boundaries clean | ✅ | — |
185	| No circular dependencies | ✅ | — |
186	| Abstraction level appropriate | ✅ | — |
187	| New deps are necessary | ✅ | — |
188	
189	### Performance
190	| Check | Status | Note |
191	|-------|--------|------|
192	| No N+1 queries | ✅ | — |
193	| Pagination present | ✅ | — |
194	| No blocking sync ops | ✅ | — |
195	| No unnecessary re-renders | ✅ | — |
196	| No unbounded loops | ✅ | — |
197	
198	### Spec Coverage
199	| Requirement | Status | Severity (if issue) | Notes |
200	|-------------|--------|---------------------|-------|
201	| REQ-1: Basic functionality | ✅ | — | Implemented and tested |
202	| REQ-2: Edge cases | ⚠️ | 🔴 Critical | Missing — no error path for null input |
203	
204	### Functional Verification
205	| Item | Result | Severity | Notes |
206	|------|--------|----------|-------|
207	| add(1,1) returns 2 | ✅ Pass | — | See test output below |
208	
209	### Tests
210	{pytest output or "No test infrastructure detected"}
211	
212	### UI Screenshots
213	{Playwright screenshots or "No UI detected"}
214	
215	### Summary
216	🔴 N Critical | 🟡 N Important | 🔵 N Suggestions | ⚪ N Nits | ℹ️ N FYI
217	```
218	
219	**g. Post Review Report to GitHub**
220	```bash
221	gh issue comment <child_number> --body "$REVIEW_REPORT"
222	```
223	
224	If screenshots were taken, upload first to get URLs, then embed them in the report markdown.
225	
226	Posting the report records evidence for the human gate. Workflow state changes happen only in the approve or reject paths in Step 6.
227	
228	### 5. Human gate: ask the user for a decision
229	
230	**This step is MANDATORY. You MUST stop here and wait for user input.**
231	
232	Use the structured question/choice tool (e.g., `question()`) to present exactly these options.
233	Do NOT present them as plain text — use the interactive selection tool so the user can click/select directly:
234	
235	1. **Approve** — commit & push all changes, move the group issue to done, and advance
236	2. **Reject** — fail this group and enter repair (no commit)
237	3. **Discuss** — talk before deciding
238	
239	Quality checks inform the decision. Only the user approves or rejects.
240	
241	**Do NOT proceed until the user explicitly chooses.**
242	
243	### 6. Advance / Repair: execute the user's decision
244	
245	**Approve, advance the group**
246	- Post a note to the child issue:
247	```bash
248	gh issue comment <child_number> --body "✅ Review passed.
249	
250	<Review Summary>"
251	```
252	- Commit and push all local changes:
253	```bash
254	git add -A
255	git commit -m "feat(<change-name>): complete Group N review"
256	git push
257	```
258	  - If there are no local changes to commit, skip and log: "No local changes to commit."
259	  - If `isolation.mode: worktree`, run git commands inside the worktree directory.
260	  - **If commit or push fails: STOP. Report the error to the user. Do NOT proceed with label changes.**
261	- Verify the child issue's current label before changing it:
262	```bash
263	gh issue view <child_number> --json labels --jq '.labels[].name'
264	```
265	  Confirm `review` is present. If not, STOP and report:
266	  "⚠️ Expected label `review` but found: \<actual labels\>. Aborting label change."
267	- Close the child issue:
268	```bash
269	gh issue edit <child_number> --remove-label "review" --add-label "done"
270	```
271	  Note: Do NOT call `gh issue close`. Closing removes issues from board label columns.
272	- Update the parent issue:
273	  - Set this group's Status to `done` in the Task Groups table
274	  - Update the `Progress:` line (example: `2/3 groups completed`)
275	```bash
276	gh issue edit <parent_number> --body "$UPDATED_PARENT_BODY"
277	```
278	
279	**Reject, enter repair**
280	1. Collect user feedback
281	   - Ask: "What's wrong? What did you expect?"
282	   - Support multiple rounds until intent is clear
283	   - Maximum 3 rounds. After that, suggest clarifying offline and re-running review later
284	2. Analyze gaps
285	   - Compare user intent vs spec vs actual implementation
286	   - Identify specific gaps: which file, which function, what is missing or wrong
287	3. Confirm fix plan
288	   - Present a concrete plan: "I plan to change: ..."
289	   - List which files will be modified and what will change
290	   - Wait for user confirmation or adjustment
291	4. Generate precise fix tasks
292	   - Convert the confirmed fix plan into `tasks.md` format
293	   - Append under the current group as `N.x` fix tasks (example: `- [ ] 1.4 Fix input validation in cli.py`)
294	   - Each fix task must be specific and actionable. Never write "fix the bug" or "improve quality"
295	5. Reset GitHub state to in-progress
296	   - Post a note to the child issue:
297	```bash
298	gh issue comment <child_number> --body "❌ Review failed.
299	
300	**Feedback:**
301	{summary of user feedback}
302	
303	**Fix Plan:**
304	{summary of proposed changes}
305	
306	**Added Tasks:**
307	- [ ] N.x fix task 1
308	- [ ] N.x fix task 2"
309	```
310	   - Verify the child issue's current label before changing it:
311	```bash
312	gh issue view <child_number> --json labels --jq '.labels[].name'
313	```
314	     Confirm `review` is present. If not, STOP and report:
315	     "⚠️ Expected label `review` but found: \<actual labels\>. Aborting label change."
316	   - Move the child issue back to in-progress:
317	```bash
318	gh issue edit <child_number> --remove-label "review" --add-label "in-progress"
319	```
320	   - Update the parent issue, set this group's Status back to `in-progress` in the Task Groups table:
321	```bash
322	gh issue edit <parent_number> --body "$UPDATED_PARENT_BODY"
323	```
324	6. Guide next steps
325	   - Tell the user: "Fix tasks have been added to tasks.md. Run `/corgi-apply` to start fixing."
326	   - Stop after task generation and state reset. Do not implement the fixes during review.
327	
328	**Discuss**
329	- Enter free-form conversation with the user
330	- The user can ask questions about the implementation, request clarification, or describe concerns
331	- The agent explains implementation logic, provides context, and offers suggestions
332	- After discussion concludes, ask the user to choose **approve** or **reject**
333	- Do not change issue labels or parent progress during discussion
334	
335	All label changes, parent updates, and repair task generation happen only inside the approve or reject paths after the user chooses.
336	
337	## Guardrails
338	
339	- Review operates on one group at a time
340	- Evidence gathering and the review report are informational. They do not decide the outcome
341	- Only the user approves or rejects
342	- Workflow state mutation happens only in the approve or reject paths
343	- Repair is limited to user feedback, gap analysis, fix plan confirmation, precise fix-task generation, state reset, and next-step guidance
344	- Review must not implement fixes
345	- If GitHub comments contain existing feedback, present them before asking for a decision
346	- All review decisions are posted back to the GitHub child issue as comments
347	- If test execution fails (infra issue, not a test failure), report the error and continue
348	- Evidence gathering is best-effort, skip gracefully if detection fails
349	- Never fabricate test results or screenshots
350	- Fix tasks must be specific and actionable
351	- Always confirm the fix plan with the user before generating tasks
352	- Repair conversation is bounded. If the user cannot articulate the issue after 3 rounds, suggest clarifying offline and re-running review later
353	
354	## Postconditions (VERIFY BEFORE REPORTING DONE)
355	
356	- [ ] Review report was posted to the GitHub child issue
357	- [ ] User explicitly chose approve, reject, or discuss (not auto-decided)
358	- [ ] If approve: all local changes committed and pushed before label change (or confirmed no changes to commit)
359	- [ ] If approve: if commit or push failed, label change was NOT performed and error was reported
360	- [ ] If approve: child issue label changed to `done` (issue left open — closing removes it from board)
361	- [ ] If approve: parent issue progress updated
362	- [ ] If reject: fix tasks added to `tasks.md`, child issue moved to `in-progress`
363	- [ ] If reject: no fixes were implemented during review
364	
365	**If you reached postconditions without asking the user in Step 5, you violated the contract. Stop and re-do Step 5.**
366	
367	## Notes
368	- Labels used on GitHub are flat: `todo`, `in-progress`, `review`, `done`
369	- Uploading screenshots can be done by attaching images in issue comments or via the GitHub API if needed
370	- Tracking file: `.github.yaml` tracks groups by their GitHub issue numbers
371	
372	(End of file)
373

1	---
2	name: corgispec-gh-propose
3	description: Propose a new change with all artifacts generated in one step and tracked via GitHub issues. Use when the user wants to quickly describe what they want to build and get a complete proposal with design, specs, and tasks ready for implementation.
4	license: MIT
5	compatibility: Requires corgispec CLI.
6	metadata:
7	  author: openspec
8	  version: "1.0"
9	  generatedBy: "1.3.0"
10	---
11	
12	Propose a new change - create the change and generate all artifacts in one step.
13	
14	I'll create a change with artifacts:
15	- proposal.md (what & why)
16	- design.md (how)
17	- tasks.md (implementation steps)
18	
19	After explicit review of the proposal/spec/design/tasks package, continue with /corgi-apply.
20	
21	---
22	
23	**Input**: The user's request should include a change name (kebab-case) OR a description of what they want to build.
24	
25	**Steps**
26	
27	1. **If no clear input provided, ask what they want to build**
28	
29	   Use the **AskUserQuestion tool** (open-ended, no preset options) to ask:
30	   > "What change do you want to work on? Describe what you want to build or fix."
31	
32	   From their description, derive a kebab-case name (e.g., "add user authentication" → `add-user-auth`).
33	
34	   **IMPORTANT**: Do NOT proceed without understanding what the user wants to build.
35	
36	2. **Check isolation mode and set up worktree (if configured)**
37	
38	   Read `openspec/config.yaml` and check for `isolation` settings:
39	
40	   ```yaml
41	   # Worktree isolation config (optional)
42	   isolation:
43	     mode: worktree    # worktree | none (default: none)
44	     root: .worktrees  # worktree root directory (default: .worktrees)
45	     branch_prefix: feat/  # feature branch prefix (default: feat/)
46	   ```
47	
48	   **If `isolation.mode` is `worktree`:**
49	   - Derive worktree path: `<root>/<name>` (e.g., `.worktrees/add-fart-tracking`)
50	   - Derive branch name: `<branch_prefix><name>` (e.g., `feat/add-fart-tracking`)
51	   - Check if the worktree already exists:
52	     ```bash
53	     git worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null | grep "worktree.*/<name>$"
54	     ```
55	   - If worktree exists → reuse it (announce: `Reusing existing worktree at <path>`)
56	   - If worktree does not exist → create it:
57	     ```bash
58	     git worktree add <root>/<name> -b <branch_prefix><name>
59	     ```
60	   - **From this point on, ALL subsequent steps run inside the worktree.** Use the Bash tool's `workdir` parameter set to the absolute worktree path for every command. File reads and writes also use absolute paths within the worktree.
61	   - Announce: `Worktree created at <path> (branch: <branch_name>)`
62	
63	   **If `isolation.mode` is `none` or `isolation` section is missing:**
64	   - Continue as today — work in the current directory
65	    - Skip the worktree-only closeout step below (Step 9)
66	
67	3. **Check for an existing change directory and issue tracking**
68	
69	   Before running `openspec new change`, check whether `openspec/changes/<name>/` already exists.
70	
71	   - If the change exists and has `.github.yaml`, announce that GitHub tracking is already configured and skip GitHub issue creation later.
72	   - If the change exists without `.github.yaml`, reuse the change directory and allow Step 6 to create issues later.
73	    - If the change does not exist, continue to Step 4.
74	
75	4. **Create or reuse the change directory**
76	   ```bash
77	   openspec new change "<name>"
78	   ```
79	   If the change does not already exist, this creates a scaffolded change at `openspec/changes/<name>/` with `.openspec.yaml`.
80	   If it already exists, reuse the existing change directory instead of creating a new one.
81	
82	5. **Develop: Get the artifact build order and build the artifact package**
83	   ```bash
84	   openspec status --change "<name>" --json
85	   ```
86	   Parse the JSON to get:
87	   - `applyRequires`: array of artifact IDs needed before implementation (e.g., `["tasks"]`)
88	   - `artifacts`: list of all artifacts with their status and dependencies
89	
90	6. **Create artifacts in sequence until all implementation-required artifacts are complete**
91	
92	   Use the **TodoWrite tool** to track progress through the artifacts.
93	
94	   Loop through artifacts in dependency order (artifacts with no pending dependencies first):
95	
96	   a. **For each artifact that is `ready` (dependencies satisfied)**:
97	      - Get instructions:
98	        ```bash
99	        openspec instructions <artifact-id> --change "<name>" --json
100	        ```
101	      - The instructions JSON includes:
102	        - `context`: Project background (constraints for you - do NOT include in output)
103	        - `rules`: Artifact-specific rules (constraints for you - do NOT include in output)
104	        - `template`: The structure to use for your output file
105	        - `instruction`: Schema-specific guidance for this artifact type
106	        - `outputPath`: Where to write the artifact
107	        - `dependencies`: Completed artifacts to read for context
108	      - Read any completed dependency files for context
109	      - Create the artifact file using `template` as the structure
110	      - Apply `context` and `rules` as constraints - but do NOT copy them into the file
111	      - Show brief progress: "Created <artifact-id>"
112	
113	    b. **Continue until all `applyRequires` artifacts are complete**
114	       - After creating each artifact, re-run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json`
115	       - Check if every artifact ID in `applyRequires` has `status: "done"` in the artifacts array
116	       - Stop when all `applyRequires` artifacts are done
117	
118	   c. **If an artifact requires user input** (unclear context):
119	      - Use **AskUserQuestion tool** to clarify
120	      - Then continue with creation
121	
122	    The primary output of propose is the completed planning artifact package: `proposal -> {spec, design} -> tasks`.
123	
124	7. **Closeout: Show final status and prepare handoff state**
125	    ```bash
126	    openspec status --change "<name>"
127	    ```
128	
129	    After the artifacts are complete, prepare the local handoff state that later phases consume. The planning artifact package remains the primary output; tracker setup and worktree metadata are closeout work layered on top of it.
130	
131	8. **Closeout: Create GitHub issues (if gh available and tracking not already configured)**
132	
133	   a. Check gh:
134	      ```bash
135	      gh auth status 2>&1
136	      ```
137	
138	   b. If the change already has `.github.yaml`, skip issue creation.
139	
140	   c. If gh is available and tracking is not yet configured:
141	      - Read `proposal.md` and `tasks.md`
142	      - Parse each `## N. Group Name` heading in `tasks.md` and its child checkbox items
143	      - Build one parent issue body with:
144	        - `**Objectives**` from the proposal's Why section
145	        - `**Background**` from the proposal's What Changes section
146	        - `**Acceptance Criteria**` — for each spec file in `specs/**/*.md`, extract each `### Requirement:` name and its first `#### Scenario:` as a one-line bullet. Format: `- **Requirement name**: WHEN condition → THEN outcome`
147	        - `**Key Design Decisions**` — from `design.md`, extract each `### N. Decision Title` heading and its `**Decision:**` line as a bullet. Format: `- **Decision heading**: decision text`. If `design.md` doesn't exist, omit this section.
148	        - `**Task Groups**` table with a Status column:
149	          ```
150	          | Group | Name | Issue | Status |
151	          |-------|------|-------|--------|
152	          | 1 | Setup | #<child_1_number> | backlog |
153	          | 2 | Core Implementation | #<child_2_number> | backlog |
154	          ```
155	          All groups start with Status `backlog`. Status values: `backlog` → `in-progress` → `review` → `done`.
156	        - `**Progress:**` 0/N groups completed
157	        - `**Child Issues**` — task list: `- [ ] #<number> Group N: name`
158	        - `**Conclusion**`
159	        - `**References**` including the change path
160	      - Create the parent issue:
161	        ```bash
162	        gh issue create --title "feat(<scope>): <change-name>" --body "$PARENT_BODY" --label "backlog"
163	        ```
164	      - For each Task Group, build a child issue body using the doc-conv#32 style sections:
165	        - `**Objectives**`
166	        - `**Todo**`
167	        - `**Estimated Completion Date:** Set when the issue is created`
168	        - `**Conclusion**`
169	        - `**References**` with the parent issue and change path
170	      - Create one child issue per Task Group:
171	        ```bash
172	        gh issue create --title "Group N: <group-name> [<change-name>]" --body "$CHILD_BODY" --label "todo"
173	        ```
174	      - Update the parent issue description so its Task Groups table and Child Issues task list includes the created child issue numbers
175	        ```bash
176	        gh issue edit <parent_issue_number> --body "$UPDATED_PARENT_BODY"
177	        ```
178	       - Save `.github.yaml` in the change directory with the canonical nested tracking contract:
179	         ```yaml
180	        parent:
181	          number: <parent_issue_number>
182	          url: <parent_issue_url>
183	        groups:
184	          - number: 1
185	            name: "Setup"
186	            issue_number: <group_1_issue_number>
187	            url: <group_1_issue_url>
188	          - number: 2
189	            name: "Core"
190	            issue_number: <group_2_issue_number>
191	            url: <group_2_issue_url>
192	        ```
193	        Later phases should treat `.github.yaml` as the canonical local tracking state. Read `parent.number` for the parent issue and match `groups[].number` to each Task Group to find `groups[].issue_number` and `url`.
194	      - Post an initial note on the parent issue:
195	        ```bash
196	        gh issue comment <parent_issue_number> --body "Planning complete. This change has one parent issue and one child issue per Task Group. Review the proposal/spec/design/tasks package. After explicit approval, run /corgi-apply to begin implementation."
197	        ```
198	      - Update `proposal.md` in the `## GitHub Issue` section with the parent issue link
199	
200	9. **Closeout: Save worktree metadata (if isolation mode is worktree)**
201	
202	    If worktree isolation is active (from Step 2), write `.worktree.yaml` in the change directory (`openspec/changes/<name>/.worktree.yaml`):
203	   ```yaml
204	   path: .worktrees/<name>
205	   branch: feat/<name>
206	   created: <ISO-8601-timestamp>
207	   ```
208	
209	   Also add worktree info to the parent issue. In the parent issue body's **References** section, include:
210	   ```markdown
211	   - Worktree: `.worktrees/<name>` (branch: `feat/<name>`)
212	   ```
213	    Update the parent issue description:
214	    ```bash
215	    gh issue edit <parent_issue_number> --body "$UPDATED_PARENT_WITH_WORKTREE"
216	    ```
217	
218	   d. If gh is unavailable:
219	      - Print a warning that GitHub issue creation is being skipped
220	      - Do not block artifact creation or readiness for explicit review
221	
222	**Output**
223	
224	After completing all artifacts, summarize:
225	- Change name and location
226	- List of artifacts created with brief descriptions
227	- Handoff status: local artifact package complete
228	- GitHub tracking status: parent issue created or skipped
229	- Worktree status: path and branch (if isolation active), or "none" (if isolation inactive)
230	- Prompt: "Review the proposal/spec/design/tasks package. After explicit approval, run `/corgi-apply` to start implementation."
231	
232	**Artifact Creation Guidelines**
233	
234	- Follow the `instruction` field from `openspec instructions` for each artifact type
235	- The schema defines what each artifact should contain - follow it
236	- Read dependency artifacts for context before creating new ones
237	- Use `template` as the structure for your output file - fill in its sections
238	- **IMPORTANT**: `context` and `rules` are constraints for YOU, not content for the file
239	  - Do NOT copy `<context>`, `<rules>`, `<project_context>` blocks into the artifact
240	  - These guide what you write, but should never appear in the output
241	
242	**Guardrails**
243	- Create ALL artifacts needed for implementation (as defined by schema's `apply.requires`)
244	- Always read dependency artifacts before creating a new one
245	- If context is critically unclear, ask the user - but prefer making reasonable decisions to keep momentum
246	- Reuse an existing change when appropriate; do not blindly fail on an existing change directory
247	- If `.github.yaml` already exists, do not create duplicate issues
248	- Verify each artifact file exists after writing before proceeding to next
249	
250	Successful artifact creation means planning and closeout are complete. It does not replace explicit human review of the proposal/spec/design/tasks package before implementation begins.
251

15	
16	**Steps**
17	
18	1. **Select change and resolve worktree**
19

21	
22	   **If `isolation.mode: worktree`**: Changes live inside worktrees, not the main checkout. Read `references/worktree-discovery.md` for the full discovery procedure. Quick summary:
23	   1. `openspec list --json` — if it returns changes, use them
24	   2. If empty (new session from main checkout): scan `<isolation.root>/` directories, verify each with `git worktree list` and check `openspec/changes/<name>/` exists inside
25	   3. Auto-select if one found, prompt if multiple

27	
28	   **If no isolation**: `openspec list --json` directly. Auto-select if one, prompt if multiple.
29	
30	   If name provided by user, use it directly.
31	
32	   **If `isolation.mode` is `none` or missing:** continue as today.
33	
34	2. **Check artifact completion status**
35	
36	   Run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json` and warn if artifacts are incomplete.
37	
38	3. **Check task completion status**
39	
40	   Read `tasks.md` if it exists. Warn if incomplete tasks remain.
41	
42	4. **Assess delta spec sync state**
43	
44	   Check for delta specs at `openspec/changes/<name>/specs/` and prompt whether to sync before archive.
45	
46	4.5 **Update GitLab issues (if tracked)**
47	
48	   Read `openspec/changes/<name>/.gitlab.yaml` BEFORE archiving moves it.
49	
50	   If tracking exists:
51	   - For each child issue, verify its current labels before changing:
52	     ```bash
53	     glab issue view <child_iid> --output json | jq -r '.labels[]'
54	     ```
55	     If the child already has `workflow::done`, skip the label change for that child.
56	     If the child has none of `workflow::todo`, `workflow::in-progress`, or `workflow::review`, STOP and report:
57	     "⚠️ Child issue #\<child_iid\> has unexpected labels: \<actual labels\>. Aborting."
58	     Otherwise proceed:
59	      ```bash
60	      glab issue update <child_iid> --unlabel "workflow::todo,workflow::in-progress,workflow::review" --label "workflow::done"
61	      ```
62	      Note: Do NOT close the issue. Closing removes issues from board label columns.
63	   - Post a final note on the parent issue:
64	      ```bash
65	      glab issue note <parent_iid> --message "Change '<name>' archived. All groups done. Specs synced: <yes/no/skipped>."
66	      ```
67	   - Verify the parent issue's current labels before changing:
68	     ```bash
69	     glab issue view <parent_iid> --output json | jq -r '.labels[]'
70	     ```
71	     Confirm `workflow::backlog` is present. If not, STOP and report:
72	     "⚠️ Expected label `workflow::backlog` on parent issue but found: \<actual labels\>. Aborting label change."
73	   - Move the parent issue to done (do NOT close):
74	      ```bash
75	      glab issue update <parent_iid> --unlabel "workflow::backlog" --label "workflow::done"
76	      ```
77	
78	   If glab is unavailable or `.gitlab.yaml` is missing, skip silently.
79	
80	4.7 **Extract long-term memory (if memory structure exists)**
81	
82	   If `memory/` and `wiki/` directories exist in the project root:
83	   - Invoke the **corgispec-memory-extract** skill against the current change
84	   - This extracts reusable patterns to `wiki/patterns/`, creates a session summary at `wiki/sessions/<name>.md`, updates `wiki/hot.md` lifecycle, resets `memory/session-bridge.md`, and updates `wiki/index.md`
85	   - If memory-extract reports issues (e.g., session summary already exists), note them in the archive summary but do not block
86	   - If `memory/` or `wiki/` do not exist, skip this step silently (project may not use memory layer)
87	
88	4.8 **Wiki sync (if wiki structure exists)**
89	
90	   If `wiki/` directory exists in the project root:
91	
92	   1. **Append wiki/log.md**: Add one line in the format defined by `wiki/schema.md`:
93	      ```
94	      <today's date> | archive <change-name> | +wiki/sessions/<name>.md +wiki/patterns/<pattern-names>.md
95	      ```
96	      List all files created by memory-extract in step 4.7. If `wiki/log.md` does not exist, create it with the format header from `wiki/schema.md` Section D.
97	
98	   2. **Update _index.md files**: For each wiki file created by memory-extract:
99	      - If a session file was created → add a wikilink entry to `wiki/sessions/_index.md`
100	      - If pattern files were created → add wikilink entries to `wiki/patterns/_index.md`
101	      - Follow the format convention in the existing `_index.md` entries: `- [[filename|Title]] — date — brief description`
102	
103	   3. **Check for extractable decisions**: Scan the change's `design.md` and the session summary for decisions with independent argumentative structure (Context + Decision + Rationale present AND affects more than a single file). If found:
104	      - Create decision pages in `wiki/decisions/` with frontmatter `type: wiki`, `updated: <today>`, `status: accepted`
105	      - Add entries to `wiki/decisions/_index.md`
106	      - If no extractable decisions found, skip silently.
107	
108	   Reference `wiki/schema.md` for format rules and exemptions.
109	
110	5. **Perform the archive**
111	
112	   Create `openspec/changes/archive/` if it does not exist and move the change to `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`.
113	
114	5.5 **Clean up worktree (if isolation active)**
115	
116	   If worktree isolation is active (from step 1.3) and the worktree exists:
117	   - Remove the worktree:
118	     ```bash
119	     git worktree remove <worktree-path> --force
120	     ```
121	   - **Do NOT delete the branch.** The branch `<branch_name>` remains for the user to merge via MR.
122	   - Announce: `Worktree removed. Branch <branch_name> preserved — create an MR to merge it, or run \`git branch -d <branch_name>\` to discard.`
123	
124	6. **Display summary**
125	
126	   Show:
127	   - Change name
128	   - Schema
129	   - Archive location
130	   - Spec sync status
131	   - GitLab status if tracked
132	   - Any warnings acknowledged during archive
133	
134	**Output On Success**
135	
136	```
137	## Archive Complete
138	
139	**Change:** <change-name>
140	**Schema:** <schema-name>
141	**Archived to:** openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/
142	**Specs:** synced / skipped / no delta specs
143	**GitLab:** parent and child issues moved to done (open, not closed)
144	**Worktree:** removed (branch `<branch-name>` preserved) / not applicable
145	```
146	
147	**Guardrails**
148	- Always prompt for change selection if not provided
149	- Use `openspec status --json` for completion checking
150	- Don't block archive on warnings; inform and confirm
151	- Preserve `.openspec.yaml` and `.gitlab.yaml` by moving the full directory
152	- If delta specs exist, always assess sync before archive

2	name: corgispec-verify
3	description: Automated verification gate between apply and review — runs tests, checks spec coverage, validates lint/build. No human gate required.
4	license: MIT
5	compatibility: Requires corgispec CLI.
6	metadata:
7	  author: openspec
8	  version: "1.0"
9	  generatedBy: "1.3.0"
10	---
11	
12	Run automated verification on a completed Task Group before review. Verify assures the code works; review judges if it's good enough.
13	
14	## Preconditions (VERIFY BEFORE STARTING)
15	
16	- [ ] Change exists in `openspec/changes/<name>/`
17	- [ ] If tracked: `.gitlab.yaml` or `.github.yaml` exists with group issue numbers
18	- [ ] If `isolation.mode` is `worktree`: worktree exists for this change (error if not)
19	- [ ] At least one Task Group has all tasks complete (verify needs something to check)
20	
21	## Forbidden Actions
22	
23	- NEVER ask for human input — verify is fully automated
24	- NEVER implement fixes — flag issues, do not resolve them
25	- NEVER create or close issues — only post a report note to existing child issues
26	- NEVER change issue labels or workflow state
27	- NEVER fabricate test results or evidence
28	- NEVER add Playwright/UI screenshots (those belong in review, not verify)
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Steps
33	
34	### 1. Discover: select change and resolve worktree
35	
36	Read `openspec/config.yaml` for schema (gitlab-tracked / github-tracked) and `isolation` settings.
37	
38	**If `isolation.mode: worktree`**: Changes live inside worktrees. Read `references/worktree-discovery.md` for the full discovery procedure. Quick summary:
39	1. `openspec list --json`, if it returns changes, use them
40	2. If empty: scan `<isolation.root>/` directories, verify each with `git worktree list` and check `openspec/changes/<name>/` exists inside
41	3. Auto-select if one found, prompt if multiple
42	4. ALL subsequent work uses the worktree as workdir
43	
44	**If no isolation**: `openspec list --json` directly. Auto-select if one, prompt if multiple.
45	
46	If name provided by user, use it directly.
47	
48	### 2. Discover: select completed Task Group
49	
50	Parse `tasks.md` to find all Task Groups (`## N.` headings). Identify which groups have ALL tasks marked `[x]`. These are the completed groups eligible for verification.
51	
52	If tracked: read the tracking file (`.gitlab.yaml` / `.github.yaml`) for group names and issue numbers.
53	
54	Default to the first completed group that hasn't been verified yet. If no completed groups exist, guidance: "No completed groups found. Run `/corgi-apply` first."
55	
56	### 3. Automated Test Execution
57	
58	Detect the project's test infrastructure and run the test suite. All detection is best-effort — skip gracefully if nothing is found.
59	
60	Use the detection table in `references/verification-steps.md` for detailed detection conditions and commands. Summary:
61	
62	| Detection Condition | Run Command | Failure Handling |
63	|---------------------|-------------|-----------------|
64	| `tests/` + `pytest.ini` / `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.pytest]` | `python -m pytest -v` | If tests fail → mark 🟡 Important, do NOT block |
65	| `package.json` with `"test"` script | `npm test` | Same as above |
66	| `bun test` exists or `bunfig.toml` | `bun test` | Same as above |
67	| `go.mod` + `_test.go` files | `go test ./...` | Same as above |
68	| No test infrastructure | Report "No test infrastructure detected", mark ⚠️, do not block |
69	
70	**Test result handling**:
71	- All tests pass → ✅ output captured, continue
72	- Some tests fail → capture failure output, mark 🟡 Important, continue
73	- No test infrastructure → mark ⚠️, note in report, continue
74	
75	Tests are evidence. Failure is a signal, not a gate.
76	
77	### 4. Spec Coverage Verification
78	
79	Compare the change's spec requirements against the actual implementation.
80	
81	Steps:
82	1. Read the spec file(s) from `openspec/changes/<name>/specs/<capability>/spec.md`
83	2. If no spec exists: note "No spec found for this group", mark ℹ️, skip
84	3. For each Requirement in the spec, check:
85	   - Is there corresponding implementation code that fulfills this requirement?
86	   - Do the Scenario behaviors map to actual code paths?
87	4. Classify each requirement:
88	   - **✅ Full**: Implementation covers all scenarios with evidence (specific file:function references)
89	   - **⚠️ Partial**: Some scenarios covered, some missing or untestable
90	   - **❌ Missing**: No implementation found for this requirement
91	
92	Output format follows the spec in `references/verification-steps.md`.
93	
94	### 5. Lint / Build Verification
95	
96	Check for project-level lint and build configuration. Run what's available.
97	
98	**Lint detection**:
99	| Condition | Command |
100	|-----------|---------|
101	| `.ruff.toml` or `[tool.ruff]` in `pyproject.toml` | `ruff check` |
102	| `.eslintrc.*` or `eslint` in `package.json` | `npx eslint .` (or configured path) |
103	| `tsconfig.json` | `npx tsc --noEmit` |
104	| No linter found | Skip, mark ℹ️ |
105	
106	**Build detection**:
107	| Condition | Command |
108	|-----------|---------|
109	| `package.json` with `"build"` script | `npm run build` |
110	| `Makefile` with `build` target | `make build` |
111	| No build config | Skip, mark ℹ️ |
112	
113	**Result handling**:
114	- Lint/build passes → ✅ captured, continue
115	- Lint/build fails → capture output, mark 🟡 Important, continue
116	- No config found → mark ℹ️, note, continue
117	
118	### 6. Generate Verify Report
119	
120	Assemble all verification results into a structured report. Read `references/verification-steps.md` for detailed report composition guidance.
121	
122	Report format (for terminal display and issue posting):
123	
124	```markdown
125	## Verify Report: Group N, {group name}
126	
127	### Test Results
128	✅ 12 passed / ❌ 0 failed / ⚠️ 2 skipped
129	
130	<test output or "No test infrastructure detected">
131	
132	### Spec Coverage
133	| Requirement | Coverage | Evidence |
134	|-------------|----------|----------|
135	| REQ-1: User login | ✅ Full | Implemented in auth/login.py:login() |
136	| REQ-2: Error handling | ⚠️ Partial | Happy path covered, null input not handled |
137	| REQ-3: Rate limiting | ❌ Missing | No rate limiting found in codebase |
138	
139	**Summary**: ✅ 2/3 fully covered | ⚠️ 1 partial | ❌ 0 missing
140	
141	### Lint / Build
142	✅ ruff: no errors | ✅ Build: success
143	
144	### Verdict
145	✅ **PASS** — Ready for review
146	```
147	
148	#### Verdict Determination
149	
150	- **✅ PASS**: All detectable checks passed (tests pass, spec fully covered, lint clean, build successful)
151	- **⚠️ PASS WITH WARNINGS**: Some checks have warnings (partial spec coverage, test failures, lint warnings) — not blocking, but noted
152	- **❌ FAIL**: Critical issues found that MUST be fixed before review (e.g., build broken, zero spec coverage for core requirements, security red flags from security checklist)
153	
154	### 7. Gate Decision and Next-Steps Guidance
155	
156	Based on the verdict from Step 6:
157	
158	**If ✅ PASS or ⚠️ PASS WITH WARNINGS**:
159	- Post the verify report to the child issue (if tracked):
160	  - GitLab: `glab issue note <child_iid> --message "$VERIFY_REPORT"`
161	  - GitHub: `gh issue comment <child_number> --body "$VERIFY_REPORT"`
162	- Print guidance: `Run /corgi-review to review this group.`
163	- If warnings present, also print: `N warnings were found. They are noted in the report but do not block review.`
164	
165	**If ❌ FAIL**:

105

107	```

116	- [ ] `openspec instructions apply --change "<name>" --json` reflects updated progress
117	- [ ] If tracked: child issue moved to review label, description updated with rich summary
118	- [ ] If tracked: parent issue progress updated

120	- [ ] If `isolation.mode` is `worktree`: all changes are in the worktree, not main checkout
121	- [ ] No fabricated file lists — only actually created/modified files reported
122	
123	**If ANY postcondition fails, STOP and report which one failed. Do not claim completion.**
124

126	
127	## Guardrails
128	
129	- Execute ONE Task Group per invocation
130	- Pause on errors, blockers, or unclear requirements — don't guess
131	- If implementation reveals design issues, suggest artifact updates
132	- Rich summaries come from actual implementation, never fabricated
133	- If `proposal.md` or `specs/` is missing, derive objectives from task descriptions

87	| "我寫的我知道它是對的" (I wrote it, I know it's right) | Authors have blind spots about their own assumptions. Every piece of code needs another pair of eyes. |
88	| "AI 生成的應該沒問題" (AI-generated code should be fine) | AI code needs MORE scrutiny, not less. It is confident and plausible but can be wrong. |
89	| "測試有過就好" (Tests pass = good enough) | Tests are necessary but insufficient. They don't catch architecture issues, security holes, or readability problems. |
90	| "以後再整理" (I'll clean it up later) | "Later" never comes. Review is the quality gate — demand cleanup now. |
91	| "Review 太花時間" (Review takes too much time) | The cost of fixing unreviewed bugs is 10x the cost of catching them in review. |
92	
93	**Severity Classification**
94	
95	Tag EVERY finding with a severity level:
96	
97	| Level | Marker | Definition | Example |
98	|-------|--------|------------|---------|
99	| **Critical** | 🔴 | Must fix to approve | Security holes, data loss risk, core feature broken |
100	| **Important** | 🟡 | Should fix or discuss before approve | Missing tests, poor error handling, spec non-compliance |
101	| **Suggestion** | 🔵 | Improvement, not required | Better naming, optional refactor, cleaner abstraction |
102	| **Nit** | ⚪ | Style preference, ignorable | Whitespace, formatting, personal taste |
103	| **FYI** | ℹ️ | Informational, no action needed | Future considerations, context notes |
104	
105	When in doubt between two levels, choose the HIGHER severity.
106	
107	**a. Code Quality Review**
108	- Read all files produced by this group (from the child issue Rich Summary's file table)
109	- Check: code structure, obvious bugs or anti-patterns, naming and style consistency
110	- Produce: a short comment per file with severity-tagged status (🔴/🟡/🔵/⚪/ℹ️)
111	
112	**b. Spec Verification**
113	- Read the corresponding `specs/<capability>/spec.md` from the change directory
114	- If no specs exist: note "No spec found for this group", skip this check
115	- Check each Requirement against the actual implementation
116	- Produce: coverage status per requirement with severity tag for any gaps
117	
118	**c. Functional Verification**
119	
120	Detect the project type and gather evidence accordingly. All detection is best-effort, skip gracefully if not applicable.
121	
122	- **Test infrastructure detection**:
123	  - Check for `tests/` directory plus `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.pytest]`, or `setup.cfg`
124	  - If found: run `python -m pytest` (or the appropriate test command), capture output
125	  - If not found: note "No test infrastructure detected", skip
126	- **UI detection**:
127	  - Check for web/frontend files (`.html`, `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.jsx`, etc.)
128	  - If found: use Playwright to open the application and capture key screenshots
129	  - Upload screenshots to GitHub by attaching them in issue comments or via API if needed
130	  - If not found: skip
131	- **CLI detection**:
132	  - Check for CLI entry points (`pyproject.toml` `[project.scripts]`, `bin/`, etc.)
133	  - If found: run basic CLI commands, capture output as evidence
134	  - If not found: skip
135	- **Fallback**: if none of the above apply, try to import or execute the core function to verify basic functionality
136	
137	**d. Architecture Check**
138	
139	Review the implementation against system design principles:
140	
141	- Does the change follow existing design patterns? If a new pattern is introduced, is it intentional and documented?
142	- Are module boundaries clean? No circular dependencies?
143	- Is the abstraction level appropriate? (Not too high, not too low — testable and composable)
144	- Are newly introduced dependencies necessary and justified?
145	
146	Produce: status per check item with severity tag for any violations.
147	
148	**e. Performance Check**
149	
150	Identify common performance anti-patterns in the implementation:
151	
152	- Data access: Any N+1 query patterns? (Check for queries inside loops)
153	- API endpoints: Any list endpoints missing pagination?
154	- Async/Sync: Any operations that should be asynchronous but are synchronous?
155	- Frontend: Any unnecessary re-renders? (React: missing useMemo/useCallback; check render-triggering state changes)
156	- Memory/CPU: Any unbounded loops or potential memory leaks? (Missing cleanup in useEffect, unclosed streams)
157	
158	Produce: status per check item with severity tag for any findings.
159	
160	> **Core principle**: Measure before optimizing. Flag patterns, do not prescribe specific optimizations without benchmark data.
161	
162	For deeper checks, the review skill also provides `references/security-checklist.md` and `references/performance-checklist.md` if more scrutiny is warranted.
163	
164	**f. Assemble Review Report**
165	
166	Format for terminal display and GitHub issue:
167	```markdown
168	## Review Report: Group N, {group name}
169	
170	### Anti-Rationalization Check
171	Confirmed no excuses are influencing review judgment:
172	- [x] "It runs" — Review covers readability, architecture, security, performance
173	- [x] "Small change" — All changes reviewed regardless of size
174	
175	### Code Quality
176	| File | Finding | Severity | Comment |
177	|------|---------|----------|---------|
178	| path/file.py | Clean structure, consistent naming | ℹ️ | — |
179	
180	### Architecture
181	| Check | Status | Note |
182	|-------|--------|------|
183	| Follows existing patterns | ✅ | — |
184	| Module boundaries clean | ✅ | — |
185	| No circular dependencies | ✅ | — |
186	| Abstraction level appropriate | ✅ | — |
187	| New deps are necessary | ✅ | — |
188	
189	### Performance
190	| Check | Status | Note |
191	|-------|--------|------|
192	| No N+1 queries | ✅ | — |
193	| Pagination present | ✅ | — |
194	| No blocking sync ops | ✅ | — |
195	| No unnecessary re-renders | ✅ | — |
196	| No unbounded loops | ✅ | — |
197	
198	### Spec Coverage
199	| Requirement | Status | Severity (if issue) | Notes |
200	|-------------|--------|---------------------|-------|
201	| REQ-1: Basic functionality | ✅ | — | Implemented and tested |
202	| REQ-2: Edge cases | ⚠️ | 🔴 Critical | Missing — no error path for null input |
203	
204	### Functional Verification
205	| Item | Result | Severity | Notes |
206	|------|--------|----------|-------|
207	| add(1,1) returns 2 | ✅ Pass | — | See test output below |
208	
209	### Tests
210	{pytest output or "No test infrastructure detected"}
211	
212	### UI Screenshots
213	{Playwright screenshots or "No UI detected"}
214	
215	### Summary
216	🔴 N Critical | 🟡 N Important | 🔵 N Suggestions | ⚪ N Nits | ℹ️ N FYI
217	```
218	
219	**g. Post Review Report to GitHub**
220	```bash
221	gh issue comment <child_number> --body "$REVIEW_REPORT"
222	```
223	
224	If screenshots were taken, upload first to get URLs, then embed them in the report markdown.
225	
226	Posting the report records evidence for the human gate. Workflow state changes happen only in the approve or reject paths in Step 6.
227	
228	### 5. Human gate: ask the user for a decision
229	
230	**This step is MANDATORY. You MUST stop here and wait for user input.**
231	
232	Use the structured question/choice tool (e.g., `question()`) to present exactly these options.
233	Do NOT present them as plain text — use the interactive selection tool so the user can click/select directly:
234	
235	1. **Approve** — commit & push all changes, move the group issue to done, and advance
236	2. **Reject** — fail this group and enter repair (no commit)
237	3. **Discuss** — talk before deciding
238	
239	Quality checks inform the decision. Only the user approves or rejects.
240	
241	**Do NOT proceed until the user explicitly chooses.**
242	
243	### 6. Advance / Repair: execute the user's decision
244	
245	**Approve, advance the group**
246	- Post a note to the child issue:
247	```bash
248	gh issue comment <child_number> --body "✅ Review passed.
249	
250	<Review Summary>"
251	```
252	- Commit and push all local changes:
253	```bash
254	git add -A
255	git commit -m "feat(<change-name>): complete Group N review"
256	git push
257	```
258	  - If there are no local changes to commit, skip and log: "No local changes to commit."
259	  - If `isolation.mode: worktree`, run git commands inside the worktree directory.
260	  - **If commit or push fails: STOP. Report the error to the user. Do NOT proceed with label changes.**
261	- Verify the child issue's current label before changing it:
262	```bash
263	gh issue view <child_number> --json labels --jq '.labels[].name'
264	```
265	  Confirm `review` is present. If not, STOP and report:
266	  "⚠️ Expected label `review` but found: \<actual labels\>. Aborting label change."
267	- Close the child issue:
268	```bash
269	gh issue edit <child_number> --remove-label "review" --add-label "done"
270	```
271	  Note: Do NOT call `gh issue close`. Closing removes issues from board label columns.
272	- Update the parent issue:
273	  - Set this group's Status to `done` in the Task Groups table
274	  - Update the `Progress:` line (example: `2/3 groups completed`)
275	```bash
276	gh issue edit <parent_number> --body "$UPDATED_PARENT_BODY"
277	```
278	
279	**Reject, enter repair**
280	1. Collect user feedback
281	   - Ask: "What's wrong? What did you expect?"
282	   - Support multiple rounds until intent is clear
283	   - Maximum 3 rounds. After that, suggest clarifying offline and re-running review later
284	2. Analyze gaps
285	   - Compare user intent vs spec vs actual implementation
286	   - Identify specific gaps: which file, which function, what is missing or wrong
287	3. Confirm fix plan
288	   - Present a concrete plan: "I plan to change: ..."
289	   - List which files will be modified and what will change
290	   - Wait for user confirmation or adjustment
291	4. Generate precise fix tasks
292	   - Convert the confirmed fix plan into `tasks.md` format
293	   - Append under the current group as `N.x` fix tasks (example: `- [ ] 1.4 Fix input validation in cli.py`)
294	   - Each fix task must be specific and actionable. Never write "fix the bug" or "improve quality"
295	5. Reset GitHub state to in-progress
296	   - Post a note to the child issue:
297	```bash
298	gh issue comment <child_number> --body "❌ Review failed.
299	
300	**Feedback:**
301	{summary of user feedback}
302	
303	**Fix Plan:**
304	{summary of proposed changes}
305	
306	**Added Tasks:**
307	- [ ] N.x fix task 1
308	- [ ] N.x fix task 2"
309	```
310	   - Verify the child issue's current label before changing it:
311	```bash
312	gh issue view <child_number> --json labels --jq '.labels[].name'
313	```
314	     Confirm `review` is present. If not, STOP and report:
315	     "⚠️ Expected label `review` but found: \<actual labels\>. Aborting label change."
316	   - Move the child issue back to in-progress:
317	```bash
318	gh issue edit <child_number> --remove-label "review" --add-label "in-progress"
319	```
320	   - Update the parent issue, set this group's Status back to `in-progress` in the Task Groups table:
321	```bash
322	gh issue edit <parent_number> --body "$UPDATED_PARENT_BODY"
323	```
324	6. Guide next steps
325	   - Tell the user: "Fix tasks have been added to tasks.md. Run `/corgi-apply` to start fixing."
326	   - Stop after task generation and state reset. Do not implement the fixes during review.
327	
328	**Discuss**
329	- Enter free-form conversation with the user
330	- The user can ask questions about the implementation, request clarification, or describe concerns
331	- The agent explains implementation logic, provides context, and offers suggestions
332	- After discussion concludes, ask the user to choose **approve** or **reject**
333	- Do not change issue labels or parent progress during discussion
334	
335	All label changes, parent updates, and repair task generation happen only inside the approve or reject paths after the user chooses.
336	
337	## Guardrails
338	
339	- Review operates on one group at a time
340	- Evidence gathering and the review report are informational. They do not decide the outcome
341	- Only the user approves or rejects
342	- Workflow state mutation happens only in the approve or reject paths
343	- Repair is limited to user feedback, gap analysis, fix plan confirmation, precise fix-task generation, state reset, and next-step guidance
344	- Review must not implement fixes
345	- If GitHub comments contain existing feedback, present them before asking for a decision
346	- All review decisions are posted back to the GitHub child issue as comments
347	- If test execution fails (infra issue, not a test failure), report the error and continue
348	- Evidence gathering is best-effort, skip gracefully if detection fails
349	- Never fabricate test results or screenshots
350	- Fix tasks must be specific and actionable
351	- Always confirm the fix plan with the user before generating tasks
352	- Repair conversation is bounded. If the user cannot articulate the issue after 3 rounds, suggest clarifying offline and re-running review later
353	
354	## Postconditions (VERIFY BEFORE REPORTING DONE)
355	
356	- [ ] Review report was posted to the GitHub child issue
357	- [ ] User explicitly chose approve, reject, or discuss (not auto-decided)
358	- [ ] If approve: all local changes committed and pushed before label change (or confirmed no changes to commit)
359	- [ ] If approve: if commit or push failed, label change was NOT performed and error was reported
360	- [ ] If approve: child issue label changed to `done` (issue left open — closing removes it from board)
361	- [ ] If approve: parent issue progress updated
362	- [ ] If reject: fix tasks added to `tasks.md`, child issue moved to `in-progress`
363	- [ ] If reject: no fixes were implemented during review
364	
365	**If you reached postconditions without asking the user in Step 5, you violated the contract. Stop and re-do Step 5.**
366	
367	## Notes
368	- Labels used on GitHub are flat: `todo`, `in-progress`, `review`, `done`
369	- Uploading screenshots can be done by attaching images in issue comments or via the GitHub API if needed
370	- Tracking file: `.github.yaml` tracks groups by their GitHub issue numbers
371	
372	(End of file)
373

10	---
11	
12	Archive a completed change in the experimental workflow.
13	
14	**Input**: Optionally specify a change name. If omitted, check if it can be inferred from conversation context. If vague or ambiguous you MUST prompt for available changes.
15	
16	**Steps**
17	
18	1. **Select change and resolve worktree**
19	
20	   Read `openspec/config.yaml` for `isolation` settings.
21	
22	   **If `isolation.mode: worktree`**: Changes live inside worktrees, not the main checkout. Read `references/worktree-discovery.md` for the full discovery procedure. Quick summary:
23	   1. `openspec list --json` — if it returns changes, use them
24	   2. If empty (new session from main checkout): scan `<isolation.root>/` directories, verify each with `git worktree list` and check `openspec/changes/<name>/` exists inside
25	   3. Auto-select if one found, prompt if multiple
26	   4. ALL subsequent work uses the worktree as workdir
27	
28	   **If no isolation**: `openspec list --json` directly. Auto-select if one, prompt if multiple.
29	
30	   If name provided by user, use it directly.
31	
32	   **If `isolation.mode` is `none` or missing:** continue as today.
33	
34	2. **Check artifact completion status**
35	
36	   Run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json` and warn if artifacts are incomplete.
37	
38	3. **Check task completion status**
39	
40	   Read `tasks.md` if it exists. Warn if incomplete tasks remain.
41	
42	4. **Assess delta spec sync state**
43	
44	   Check for delta specs at `openspec/changes/<name>/specs/` and prompt whether to sync before archive.
45	
46	4.5 **Update GitLab issues (if tracked)**
47	
48	   Read `openspec/changes/<name>/.gitlab.yaml` BEFORE archiving moves it.
49	
50	   If tracking exists:
51	   - For each child issue, verify its current labels before changing:
52	     ```bash
53	     glab issue view <child_iid> --output json | jq -r '.labels[]'
54	     ```
55	     If the child already has `workflow::done`, skip the label change for that child.
56	     If the child has none of `workflow::todo`, `workflow::in-progress`, or `workflow::review`, STOP and report:
57	     "⚠️ Child issue #\<child_iid\> has unexpected labels: \<actual labels\>. Aborting."
58	     Otherwise proceed:
59	      ```bash
60	      glab issue update <child_iid> --unlabel "workflow::todo,workflow::in-progress,workflow::review" --label "workflow::done"
61	      ```
62	      Note: Do NOT close the issue. Closing removes issues from board label columns.
63	   - Post a final note on the parent issue:
64	      ```bash
65	      glab issue note <parent_iid> --message "Change '<name>' archived. All groups done. Specs synced: <yes/no/skipped>."
66	      ```
67	   - Verify the parent issue's current labels before changing:
68	     ```bash
69	     glab issue view <parent_iid> --output json | jq -r '.labels[]'
70	     ```
71	     Confirm `workflow::backlog` is present. If not, STOP and report:
72	     "⚠️ Expected label `workflow::backlog` on parent issue but found: \<actual labels\>. Aborting label change."
73	   - Move the parent issue to done (do NOT close):
74	      ```bash
75	      glab issue update <parent_iid> --unlabel "workflow::backlog" --label "workflow::done"
76	      ```
77	
78	   If glab is unavailable or `.gitlab.yaml` is missing, skip silently.
79	
80	4.7 **Extract long-term memory (if memory structure exists)**
81	
82	   If `memory/` and `wiki/` directories exist in the project root:
83	   - Invoke the **corgispec-memory-extract** skill against the current change
84	   - This extracts reusable patterns to `wiki/patterns/`, creates a session summary at `wiki/sessions/<name>.md`, updates `wiki/hot.md` lifecycle, resets `memory/session-bridge.md`, and updates `wiki/index.md`
85	   - If memory-extract reports issues (e.g., session summary already exists), note them in the archive summary but do not block
86	   - If `memory/` or `wiki/` do not exist, skip this step silently (project may not use memory layer)
87	
88	4.8 **Wiki sync (if wiki structure exists)**
89	
90	   If `wiki/` directory exists in the project root:
91	
92	   1. **Append wiki/log.md**: Add one line in the format defined by `wiki/schema.md`:
93	      ```
94	      <today's date> | archive <change-name> | +wiki/sessions/<name>.md +wiki/patterns/<pattern-names>.md
95	      ```
96	      List all files created by memory-extract in step 4.7. If `wiki/log.md` does not exist, create it with the format header from `wiki/schema.md` Section D.
97	
98	   2. **Update _index.md files**: For each wiki file created by memory-extract:
99	      - If a session file was created → add a wikilink entry to `wiki/sessions/_index.md`
100	      - If pattern files were created → add wikilink entries to `wiki/patterns/_index.md`
101	      - Follow the format convention in the existing `_index.md` entries: `- [[filename|Title]] — date — brief description`
102	
103	   3. **Check for extractable decisions**: Scan the change's `design.md` and the session summary for decisions with independent argumentative structure (Context + Decision + Rationale present AND affects more than a single file). If found:
104	      - Create decision pages in `wiki/decisions/` with frontmatter `type: wiki`, `updated: <today>`, `status: accepted`
105	      - Add entries to `wiki/decisions/_index.md`
106	      - If no extractable decisions found, skip silently.
107	
108	   Reference `wiki/schema.md` for format rules and exemptions.
109	
110	5. **Perform the archive**
111	
112	   Create `openspec/changes/archive/` if it does not exist and move the change to `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`.
113	
114	5.5 **Clean up worktree (if isolation active)**
115	
116	   If worktree isolation is active (from step 1.3) and the worktree exists:
117	   - Remove the worktree:
118	     ```bash
119	     git worktree remove <worktree-path> --force
120	     ```
121	   - **Do NOT delete the branch.** The branch `<branch_name>` remains for the user to merge via MR.
122	   - Announce: `Worktree removed. Branch <branch_name> preserved — create an MR to merge it, or run \`git branch -d <branch_name>\` to discard.`
123	
124	6. **Display summary**
125	
126	   Show:
127	   - Change name
128	   - Schema
129	   - Archive location
130	   - Spec sync status
131	   - GitLab status if tracked
132	   - Any warnings acknowledged during archive
133	
134	**Output On Success**
135	
136	```
137	## Archive Complete
138	
139	**Change:** <change-name>
140	**Schema:** <schema-name>
141	**Archived to:** openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/
142	**Specs:** synced / skipped / no delta specs
143	**GitLab:** parent and child issues moved to done (open, not closed)
144	**Worktree:** removed (branch `<branch-name>` preserved) / not applicable
145	```
146	
147	**Guardrails**
148	- Always prompt for change selection if not provided
149	- Use `openspec status --json` for completion checking
150	- Don't block archive on warnings; inform and confirm
151	- Preserve `.openspec.yaml` and `.gitlab.yaml` by moving the full directory
152	- If delta specs exist, always assess sync before archive

41	```

46	
47	**If `isolation.mode` is `none` or `isolation` section is missing:**

52	```bash

1	---
2	name: corgispec-install
3	description: Use when installing, updating, or verifying this repo's project-local OpenSpec GitFlow assets in a target project.
4	license: MIT
5	compatibility: Requires corgispec CLI.
6	metadata:
7	  author: openspec
8	  version: "1.0"

10	---
11	
12	Install, update, or verify project-local OpenSpec GitFlow assets.
13	
14	## Overview
15	
16	Use this skill to set up or maintain the repo-managed OpenSpec workflow files inside a target project.
17	
18	This installer manages:
19	- **Project-local** command dispatch files and bundled schemas (per-repo)
20	- **User-level** command dispatch files (global, so `/corgi-*` commands work in every repo)
21	
22	`corgispec-*` skills must already be installed at user level before this skill runs.
23	
24	## When to Use
25	
26	- Fresh install into a project that already ran `corgispec init`
27	- Managed update when the target project already has an installer manifest
28	- Legacy install migration when managed files exist but no installer manifest exists
29	- Verify-only when the user wants a report without mutating files
30	
31	Do not use this skill to create feature artifacts, review implementation work, or archive a change.
32	
33	## Core Pattern
34	
35	1. Inspect the target project and classify state:
36	   - Fresh install
37	   - Managed update
38	   - Legacy install
39	   - Verify-only
40	2. Ask for required choices:
41	   - target project path
42	   - schema: `gitlab-tracked` or `github-tracked`
43	   - whether to enable worktree isolation
44	3. Sync project-local managed fileset for OpenCode, Claude, and bundled schemas.
45	4. **Sync user-level commands** — copy `corgi-*.md` dispatch files to:
46	   - OpenCode: `~/.config/opencode/commands/corgi-*.md`
47	   - Claude Code: `~/.claude/commands/corgi/*.md`
48	5. Record runtime artifacts:
49	   - `openspec/.corgi-install.json`
50	   - `openspec/.corgi-install-report.md`
51	   - `openspec/.corgi-backups/<timestamp>/` when backup is needed
52	6. Stop instead of overwriting locally modified managed files (both project-local and user-level).
53	
54	Do not overwrite locally modified managed files — stop with a diff and let the user decide.
55	
56	> **Why user-level commands?** Without them, `/corgi-*` commands only exist in repos where you've run the installer. User-level install makes them available in every repo after a single installation.
57	
58	## Quick Reference
59	
60	| Mode | Mutates Files | Expected Output |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| Fresh install | Yes | managed files + manifest + report |
63	| Managed update | Yes | updated managed files + refreshed manifest + report |
64	| Legacy install | Maybe | backup prompt, then manifest + report if approved |
65	| Verify-only | Report only | report + checks, no managed-file or config mutations |
66	
67	Managed fileset (project-local):
68	- `.opencode/commands/corgi-*.md`
69	- `.claude/commands/corgi/*.md`
70	- `openspec/schemas/{selected-schema}/**`
71	
72	Managed fileset (user-level):
73	- `~/.config/opencode/commands/corgi-*.md`
74	- `~/.claude/commands/corgi/*.md`
75	
76	Required user-level skills:
77	- Claude Code: `~/.claude/skills/corgispec-*`
78	- OpenCode: `~/.config/opencode/skill/corgispec-*`
79	
80	Runtime artifacts:
81	- Manifest: `openspec/.corgi-install.json`
82	- Report: `openspec/.corgi-install-report.md`
83	- Backups: `openspec/.corgi-backups/<timestamp>/`
84	
85	## Implementation
86	
87	- Target projects must already contain `openspec/config.yaml`.
88	- Only patch installer-owned fields in `openspec/config.yaml`:
89	  - `schema`
90	  - `isolation.mode`
91	  - `isolation.root`
92	  - `isolation.branch_prefix`
93	- Prompt before enabling worktree isolation.
94	- Treat missing manifest + existing managed files as a legacy install.
95	- Verify-only must never write files or create backups.
96	- Managed update must stop if a managed file differs from the last recorded manifest hash.
97	- Treat missing user-level `corgispec-*` skills as a prerequisite failure.
98	- **User-level commands are installed unconditionally** — they are not tracked in the project manifest. On update, always refresh user-level commands from source.
99	- **Project-local commands override user-level commands** — if a project has a custom `.opencode/commands/corgi-propose.md`, it takes precedence over the user-level one. OpenCode and Claude resolve project-local before user-level.
100	
101	## Prerequisites Check
102	
103	Before any mode runs, verify the required tools are available:
104	
105	```bash
106	corgispec --version
107	```
108	
109	If the user is working with a github-tracked schema:
110	```bash
111	gh auth status
112	```
113	
114	If the user is working with a gitlab-tracked schema:
115	```bash
116	glab auth status
117	```
118	
119	Verify the required user-level skills are already installed:
120	
121	- Claude Code skills under `~/.claude/skills/corgispec-*`
122	- OpenCode skills under `~/.config/opencode/skill/corgispec-*`
123	
124	If any required tool is missing, unauthenticated, or the required user-level skills are absent, stop and report the failure in the report before proceeding. Tell the user to run the repo's global installer script before retrying.
125	
126	## Mode Steps
127	
128	### Fresh Install
129	
130	Use when the target project has no managed fileset and no manifest.
131	
132	1. **Validate prerequisites**
133	   - Run `corgispec --version` — stop if not found
134	   - Run `gh auth status` or `glab auth status` depending on intended schema — stop if unauthenticated
135	   - Verify `~/.claude/skills/corgispec-*` and `~/.config/opencode/skill/corgispec-*` exist — stop if missing
136	   - Confirm `openspec/config.yaml` exists in the target project — stop if missing
137	
138	2. **Ask for target project path**
139	   - Prompt: "What is the path to the target project?"
140	   - Resolve to an absolute path
141	   - Verify the directory exists and contains `openspec/config.yaml`
142	
143	3. **Ask for schema choice**
144	   - Prompt: "Which schema? `gitlab-tracked` or `github-tracked`"
145	   - Record the choice — it determines which schema directory to copy and which CLI to verify
146	
147	4. **Ask whether to enable worktree isolation**
148	   - Prompt: "Enable worktree isolation? (yes/no — default: no)"
149	   - If yes: ask for `isolation.root` (default: `.worktrees`) and `isolation.branch_prefix` (default: `feat/`)
150	   - Do NOT auto-enable worktree isolation without asking
151	
152	4b. **Ask whether to initialize memory structure**
153	   - Prompt: "Initialize memory structure for cross-session continuity? (yes/no — default: yes)"
154	   - If user passes `--no-memory` flag: skip this prompt and do not initialize memory
155	   - Record the choice for Step 10
156	
157	5. **Copy project-local managed fileset from source repo to target**
158	
159	   Copy each of the following from the source repo (this repo) to the target project:
160	
161	    - `.opencode/commands/corgi-*.md` → target `.opencode/commands/corgi-*.md`
162	    - `.claude/commands/corgi/*.md` → target `.claude/commands/corgi/*.md`
163	    - `openspec/schemas/{selected-schema}/**` → target `openspec/schemas/{selected-schema}/**`
164	
165	   Create destination directories as needed. Do not delete any unmanaged files in the target.
166	
167	5b. **Install user-level commands (global, all repos)**
168	
169	    Copy the same `corgi-*.md` command dispatch files to user-level directories so they are available in every repo:
170	
171	    - `.opencode/commands/corgi-*.md` → `~/.config/opencode/commands/corgi-*.md`
172	    - `.claude/commands/corgi/*.md` → `~/.claude/commands/corgi/*.md`
173	
174	    Create destination directories as needed.
175	
176	    > **Why both project-local and user-level?** Project-local files let individual repos override commands. User-level files provide the default so every repo has `/corgi-*` even without running the installer.
177	
178	6. **Patch `openspec/config.yaml`**
179	
180	   Read the existing `openspec/config.yaml` in the target project. Update only these keys:
181	   - `schema` — set to the chosen schema
182	   - `isolation.mode` — set to `worktree` or `none` based on user choice
183	   - `isolation.root` — set if worktree enabled
184	   - `isolation.branch_prefix` — set if worktree enabled
185	
186	   Do NOT replace the whole file. Preserve all other keys (e.g., `context`, `rules`).
187	
188	7. **Compute SHA-256 hashes for project-local files**
189	
190	   For each file copied in step 5 (project-local only), compute its SHA-256 hash:
191	   ```bash
192	   sha256sum <file>
193	   ```
194	   
195	   User-level commands are not hashed in the manifest — they are refreshed on every update.
196	
197	8. **Write `openspec/.corgi-install.json` manifest**
198	
199	   Write the manifest with all copied file paths and their hashes. See [Manifest Format](#manifest-format).
200	
201	9. **Generate `openspec/.corgi-install-report.md`**
202	
203	   Write the report with mode, timestamp, source repo, target project, and per-check status. See [Verification Report](#verification-report).
204	
205	10. **Initialize memory structure (unless opted out)**
206	
207	    If the user chose to initialize memory in Step 4b (or did not pass `--no-memory`):
208	    - Invoke the **corgispec-memory-init** skill against the target project
209	    - This creates `memory/` and `wiki/` directories with template files
210	    - It also injects the Session Memory Protocol into the project's agent config file
211	    - If memory-init reports files skipped (already exist), include that in the install report
212	    - If `--no-memory` was specified or user declined: skip this step entirely
213	
214	---
215	
216	### Managed Update
217	
218	Use when the target project already has `openspec/.corgi-install.json`.
219	
220	1. **Validate prerequisites**
221	   - Run `corgispec --version` — stop if not found
222	   - Run `gh auth status` or `glab auth status` as appropriate — stop if unauthenticated
223	   - Verify `~/.claude/skills/corgispec-*` and `~/.config/opencode/skill/corgispec-*` exist — stop if missing
224	
225	2. **Read existing `openspec/.corgi-install.json`**
226	   - Parse the manifest to get the list of managed files and their recorded SHA-256 hashes
227	   - Note the schema and isolation settings from the manifest
228	
229	3. **For each managed file: compare current hash vs manifest hash**
230	   - Compute the current SHA-256 of each managed file in the target project
231	   - Compare against the hash stored in the manifest
232	
233	4. **If ANY managed file differs from its manifest hash → abort**
234	   - Print a diff of the changed file(s):
235	     ```bash
236	     diff <source-file> <target-file>
237	     ```
238	   - Do not overwrite locally modified managed files
239	   - Write a FAIL status to `openspec/.corgi-install-report.md`
240	   - Stop. Tell the user which files have local modifications and ask them to resolve the conflict manually before re-running
241	
242	5. **If all managed files are clean → proceed with update**
243	   - Copy updated project-local files from source repo to target (same fileset as fresh install step 5)
244	   - **Copy updated user-level commands** (same fileset as fresh install step 5b) — always refresh unconditionally
245	   - Recompute SHA-256 hashes for all project-local files
246	   - Refresh `openspec/.corgi-install.json` with new hashes and updated `updatedAt` timestamp
247	   - Write updated `openspec/.corgi-install-report.md`
248	
249	---
250	
251	### Legacy Install
252	
253	Use when managed files exist in the target project but no `openspec/.corgi-install.json` is present.
254	
255	1. **Detect legacy state**
256	    - Managed files exist (e.g., `.opencode/commands/corgi-propose.md` is present)
257	    - `openspec/.corgi-install.json` does NOT exist
258	    - Classify as legacy install and display this classification to the user
259	
260	2. **Display legacy classification to user**
261	   - Announce: "This project has OpenSpec managed files but no installer manifest. This looks like a legacy install."
262	   - List the managed files found
263	
264	3. **Create backup**
265	   - Create a timestamped backup directory: `openspec/.corgi-backups/<timestamp>/`
266	   - Copy all currently present managed files into the backup directory, preserving relative paths
267	
268	4. **Ask user for explicit approval before migration**
269	   - Prompt: "Proceed with legacy migration? This will overwrite managed files with the current source versions. A backup has been created at `openspec/.corgi-backups/<timestamp>/`. (yes/no)"
270	   - Wait for explicit user response — do NOT auto-proceed
271	
272	5. **If approved → proceed as fresh install, then write manifest**
273	   - Follow fresh install steps 2–9 (ask for schema, worktree preference, copy files, patch config, write manifest and report)
274	
275	6. **If declined → abort, write report only**
276	   - Write `openspec/.corgi-install-report.md` with mode `legacy-install`, status `aborted`, and a note that the user declined migration
277	   - Do not modify any files
278	
279	---
280	
281	### Verify-only
282	
283	Use when the user wants a health check without any file mutations.
284	
285	1. **Check prerequisites**
286	   - Run `corgispec --version` — record PASS or FAIL
287	   - Run `gh auth status` or `glab auth status` as appropriate — record PASS, FAIL, or SKIP
288	   - Verify `~/.claude/skills/corgispec-*` and `~/.config/opencode/skill/corgispec-*` exist — record PASS or FAIL
289	
290	2. **Check project-local managed fileset presence and integrity**
291	   - For each file in the managed fileset, check whether it exists in the target project
292	   - If `openspec/.corgi-install.json` exists: also compare current SHA-256 hashes against manifest hashes
293	   - Record PASS if all present and matching, FAIL if any missing or mismatched
294	
295	2b. **Check user-level commands presence**
296	    - Check whether `~/.config/opencode/commands/corgi-*.md` and `~/.claude/commands/corgi/*.md` exist
297	    - Record PASS if all present, FAIL if any missing (WARN if user-level commands are missing but project-local ones exist — project-local will still work, but other repos won't have them)
298	
299	3. **Check `openspec/config.yaml` has required fields**
300	   - Verify `schema` field is present and set to a known value
301	   - Record PASS or FAIL
302	
303	4. **Check schema directory exists**
304	   - Verify `openspec/schemas/{schema}/` exists and contains `schema.yaml`
305	   - Record PASS or FAIL
306	
307	   5. **Write report with PASS/FAIL per check**
308	    - Write `openspec/.corgi-install-report.md` with all check results
309	    - See [Verification Report](#verification-report) for format
310	
311	    **NO managed-file mutations. NO backups. NO config changes. This mode may write the verification report only.**
312	
313	---
314	
315	## Verification Report
316	
317	The report at `openspec/.corgi-install-report.md` uses this format:
318	
319	### Header
320	- Mode: [fresh-install | managed-update | legacy-install | verify-only]
321	- Timestamp: ISO 8601
322	- Source repo: path
323	- Target project: path
324	
325	### Checks
326	| Check | Status | Detail |
327	|---|---|---|---|
328	| corgispec CLI | PASS/FAIL | version or error |
329	| gh/glab CLI | PASS/FAIL/SKIP | version or error |
330	| User-level skills | PASS/FAIL | Claude/OpenCode skill paths checked |
331	| User-level commands | PASS/FAIL/WARN | OpenCode/Claude command paths checked |
332	| Schema directory | PASS/FAIL | path checked |
333	| Config file | PASS/FAIL | fields present |
334	| Managed files | PASS/FAIL | N/M project-local files synced |
335	
336	### Summary
337	- Overall: PASS or FAIL
338	- Actions taken: [list of mutations, or "none (verify-only)"]
339	
340	For end-to-end validation scenarios covering fresh install, managed update, local modifications, verify-only, legacy install, and the worktree prompt, see `.sisyphus/plans/corgi-install-smoke-matrix.md`.
341	
342	---
343	
344	## Manifest Format
345	
346	The manifest at `openspec/.corgi-install.json`:
347	
348	```json
349	{
350	  "version": 1,
351	  "installedAt": "ISO-8601",
352	  "updatedAt": "ISO-8601",
353	  "sourceRepo": "/path/to/ds-internal-skills",
354	  "schema": "gitlab-tracked",
355	  "isolation": { "mode": "none" },
356	  "files": {
357	    ".opencode/commands/corgi-propose.md": { "sha256": "abc123..." },
358	    ".opencode/commands/corgi-install.md": { "sha256": "def456..." },
359	    ".claude/commands/corgi/propose.md": { "sha256": "ghi789..." },
360	    "openspec/schemas/gitlab-tracked/schema.yaml": { "sha256": "jkl012..." }
361	  }
362	}
363	```
364	
365	- `installedAt` — set on first write, never changed on update
366	- `updatedAt` — refreshed on every managed update
367	- `files` — keyed by path relative to the target project root; value is the SHA-256 of the file as installed
368	- **User-level commands are NOT tracked in the manifest** — they are refreshed unconditionally on every install/update
369	
370	---
371	
372	## Common Mistakes
373	
374	- Overwriting locally modified managed files instead of stopping with a diff
375	- Writing schemas or config to user-home directories (those stay project-local)
376	- Auto-enabling worktree isolation without asking
377	- Replacing the whole `openspec/config.yaml` instead of patching only managed keys
378	- Running verify-only in a mutating mode
379	- Skipping the backup step before legacy migration
380	- Forgetting to check `gh auth status` or `glab auth status` before a write operation
381	- Forgetting that `corgispec-*` skills are user-level prerequisites, not project-local managed files
382	- Running memory-init when `--no-memory` was specified
383	- Auto-initializing memory without asking the user first (unless default-yes prompt is used)
384	- Installing user-level commands but **not** installing project-local ones (project-local overrides won't work)
385	- Forgetting to refresh user-level commands on update — user-level commands are NOT hash-tracked, always refresh them

2	name: corgispec-verify
3	description: Automated verification gate between apply and review — runs tests, checks spec coverage, validates lint/build. No human gate required.
